key_insight: Raising the flame-spraying O₂/C₂H₂ ratio densified Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings, lowering porosity and roughness while improving adhesion, with peak hardness at an intermediate ratio.
engineering_relevance: Tuning the O₂/C₂H₂ ratio is a practical process-control lever for optimizing protective coating quality on AISI 321 steel in industrial flame-spraying applications.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si coatings onto AISI 321 austenitic stainless steel using a Metal Coat 6PM-II system.
Varied the O₂/C₂H₂ ratio at 1.0, 1.1, and 1.2 and monitored spraying with Accuraspray 4.0.
Measured microstructure, porosity, microhardness, surface roughness, and adhesion strength.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports clear quantitative trends across the tested ratios: porosity dropped from 1.97% to 0.90%, roughness from 4.70 to 2.99 μm, and adhesion rose from 22.14 to 35.02 MPa, with maximum microhardness of 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The optimum depends on the target property: the highest hardness occurred at 1.1, while the best porosity/roughness/adhesion combination occurred at 1.2, so process settings must match the application goal.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
